# Admin Agents — an admin dashboard of autogenerated agents

Status: implemented, 2026-08-01. Companion to
[agent-auto-registration-and-sandbox-builder.md](agent-auto-registration-and-sandbox-builder.md).

The idea in one line: **rails_admin scaffolds admin screens around
ActiveRecord models; we scaffold admin agents around them.**

A Rails app that installs the activeagent gem (with the telemetry and
solid_agent extras) already reports traces. This feature adds the second
half of the loop: the app reports its **resource manifest** — its
ActiveRecord models — and the platform generates one **admin agent per
resource**. If the app has no admin dashboard (or only a partial one),
the agents *are* the admin surface: they do the work of admin screens
through conversation and tools, in web-admin ways without the admin UI,
with a human in the loop in the operator's own browser for anything
destructive.

## The pipeline

```
connected app                        platform
─────────────                        ────────
bin/rails active_agent:              POST /v1/resources
  report_resources        ────────► (Bearer ApiKey / telemetry key)
                                        │
                                        ▼
                                    AdminResource upsert
                                    (account, service_name, name)
                                        │
                          dashboard: Admin Agents view
                          "Generate agent" / "Generate all"
                                        │
                                        ▼
                                    AdminAgentScaffold
                                        │
                                        ▼
                                    Agent record (reusable, versioned,
                                    executable, MCP-exposed)
```

## Ingestion — POST /v1/resources

A sibling of telemetry ingest on the same Bearer plane
(`IngestAuthentication` concern: dashboard ApiKey tokens or the legacy
`Account#telemetry_api_key`). The payload is a full snapshot:

```json
{
  "service_name": "support_inbox",
  "environment": "production",
  "resources": [
    {
      "name": "Ticket",
      "table_name": "tickets",
      "columns": [ { "name": "subject", "type": "string", "null": false } ],
      "associations": [ { "kind": "has_many", "name": "replies", "class_name": "Reply" } ],
      "record_count": 1042,
      "admin_route": null
    }
  ]
}
```

Rows land in `admin_resources`, keyed on **(account, service_name,
name)** — the same identity convention as agent auto-registration
(`environment` is attribution, not identity). Re-reporting refreshes
columns/associations/counts in place; a dropped column disappears on the
next report. Per-request cardinality is capped
(`MAX_RESOURCES_PER_REQUEST = 200`), per-item failures are logged and
skipped — ingest never 500s the customer.

`admin_route` is the resource's existing admin UI path when the app has
one (the reporter detects `admin_*_path` route helpers). It decides which
of two postures the generated agent takes (below).

`examples/support_inbox/lib/tasks/report_resources.rake` is the reference
reporter: ActiveRecord introspection (columns, associations, counts,
admin routes) posted with the same env vars as telemetry.

## Scaffolding — AdminAgentScaffold

`AdminAgentScaffold.call(resource, user:)` finds-or-creates an ordinary
`Agent` record — so generated agents inherit everything agents already
have: versioning, execution through `AgentExecutionService` (solid_agent
context persistence, telemetry, memory), the MCP surface, evaluations.

What the scaffold writes:

- **Identity** — name `"Ticket Admin"`, `agent_class_name`
  `"TicketAdminAgent"` (the telemetry correlation key), status `active`.
- **Instructions** — the reported schema rendered as prose (columns with
  types/nullability/defaults, associations, record count, schema
  fingerprint) plus the admin charter: check the live manifest before
  reasoning about fields, never invent data, hand off to the human for
  destructive actions, record durable observations to memory.
- **Surface rule** — two postures:
  - `admin_route` present: drive the app's admin UI in the browser like a
    careful human admin, narrating each step.
  - no admin UI: *the agent is the admin surface* — operate in web-admin
    ways without the admin UI.
- **Action prompts** — the CRUD verbs an admin dashboard renders as
  screens: `list_records`, `inspect_record`, `create_record`,
  `update_record`, `archive_record`. Read-only actions are
  `expose_as_tool: true` (so MCP clients get `run_<slug>__list_records`);
  mutating ones are deliberately not exposed — they stay behind a human
  invoking them on purpose.
- **Tools** — `database fetch playwright memory`.

Regeneration is rails_admin-like: scaffold-owned fields are overwritten
from the latest manifest (the Agent versioning callback records the
change as a new `AgentVersion`), while user-tuned fields (provider,
model, model_config, appearance) are preserved.

## The database tool

The previously config-only `database` tool key now has a server-side
implementation, subject-bound like memory (routed in
`AgentExecutionService#execute_tool` because it needs the calling agent's
account scope):

- `list_resources(service_name?)` — every reported resource: model,
  table, column/record counts, admin-UI flag.
- `describe_resource(name, service_name?)` — one resource's full
  reported schema plus fingerprint.

So an admin agent's schema knowledge isn't frozen at generation time — it
can check the live manifest mid-run.

## Human in the loop

Generated agents are built for supervised admin work, stacking on the
existing session-replay handoff machinery
([session-replay.md](session-replay.md)):

- Instructions require operator confirmation before anything destructive
  or irreversible; the agent prepares exact changes and hands off rather
  than guessing.
- Mutating actions aren't exposed as MCP tools; a human invokes them.
- Browser-driving runs record through `SessionRecordingService`, and
  `capture_handoff_state` / `POST /api/session_recordings/:id/handoff`
  hand the session to the operator in their own Chrome — the dev user
  stays logged in, the agent stops, the human continues.

## Saved to files — Active Storage

Agents and run contexts are portable artifacts, not just rows:

- `Agent#save_export_file!` attaches the full export payload (config
  snapshot, generated ActiveAgent class code, package manifest) as JSON —
  `POST /api/agents/:id/export_file`.
- `AgentContext#save_export_file!` attaches the whole run context
  (instructions, messages, generations with trace ids) —
  `POST /api/interactions/:id/export_file`.

Both follow the `RecordingSnapshot` attachment pattern (StringIO attach,
Disk service locally) and return `{filename, content_type, byte_size,
url, attached_at}` with a `rails_blob_path` download URL.

## Dashboard — Admin Agents view

`/dashboard/admin-agents` (sidebar: Agents → Admin Agents). One card per
connected service: resources table (columns/records/admin-UI posture/last
report), **Generate agent** per resource, **Generate all agents** per
service, generated-agent chip opening the editor, **Regenerate** and
**Save to file** actions. Empty state shows the rake task and a raw curl
example. `GET /api/admin_resources`, `POST /api/admin_resources/:id/generate`,
`POST /api/admin_resources/generate_all` (session-auth plane).

## Deliberate decisions

- **Account-scoped resources, user-attributed agents.** Manifests arrive
  on the Bearer plane, so `AdminResource belongs_to :account` (the
  auto-registration doc's recommendation); generation happens from a
  dashboard session, so the scaffolded Agent gets that user as author.
- **Generated agents start `active`, not `draft`** — generation is an
  explicit user action (a click), not passive observation; the
  auto-registration doc's `observed` status is for agents created by
  watching.
- **Scaffold overwrites scaffold-owned fields on regenerate.** The
  alternative (three-way merge with user edits) isn't worth it while
  `AgentVersion` history makes every overwrite recoverable.
- **No new ingest job.** Manifests are small (≤200 resources) and
  idempotent; synchronous upsert keeps the endpoint simple. Traces keep
  their async job.

## Open questions

- The database tool scopes to the agent owner's `primary_account` — the
  same workspace rule as `call_agent` and memory. When an agent is
  executed from another account's MCP key (owner is a member there), the
  tool still reads the owner's primary account. Today every account has
  one member so the planes coincide; threading the *invoking* account
  through execution is the general fix, and it's the same modelling
  decision the auto-registration doc flags as blocking.

- Should a schema change auto-regenerate agents on ingest (with the
  version history as the audit trail), or stay click-driven? Leaning:
  stay click-driven; surface staleness via `schema_fingerprint` diff in
  the UI first.
- The reporter could ship inside the activeagent gem as a railtie task
  (`active_agent:report_resources` upstream) — the example app's rake
  task is the contract reference until then.
- Sampled row values (redacted) would make create/update actions much
  smarter; deliberately excluded until there's a privacy story.
